function_question: How does a computer make a decision?

opening.text: There was a friendly robot called Pixel who loved playing guessing games.
Pixel played "guess the animal", but it asked questions like "Is it a zebra?" and "Is it a frog?" and needed ages to win.
Pixel wondered: "What if I could guess ANY animal with only a few yes/no questions? Which question should I ask first?"

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The guessing game
chapters.line: Pixel wants to win in as few questions as possible. A bad first question wastes a turn!

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Pixel asks for help
chapters.line: What is the smartest first question? Pixel needs a teammate. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: Real-world question askers
chapters.line: You and Pixel find out who else wins by asking yes/no questions.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of the tree
chapters.line: Every clue uses the same secret: a decision tree.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: The card-sorting lab
chapters.line: No magic, just cards! Pixel hands you 8 animal cards.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The question storm
chapters.line: Twenty questions in five minutes. Ready, steady, go!

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: Drawing the tree
chapters.line: Your best question goes at the top, and the branches grow down.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: Pixel plays for real
chapters.line: Five rounds, one better question, then five more rounds.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: Pixel wins in three
chapters.line: Pixel guesses any of the 8 animals in a flash.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Pixel wants to guess any animal with the fewest yes/no questions. Can you help Pixel build a question tree that finds any of 8 animals in 3 questions or fewer? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some players already know their best first question. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Computers can't "just know" an answer. They follow steps. Tap each card to meet four real-world question askers!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four clues share…
guide.skill: Unplugged first! Which question splits your 8 animal cards most evenly? Predict, then count the piles.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your question tree like a real AI designer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your tree in the Question Tree game, press Play, and count the questions it needs!
guide.retry_tip: Swap your top question for a more even one, and play 5 more rounds!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Pixel wins every guessing game with YOUR tree, the same idea that helps spam filters and game AI decide!

quick_check.question: Each perfect question splits the animals in half. How many questions to find 1 animal out of 8?
quick_check.right: Right! 8 → 4 → 2 → 1. With perfect half-splits, 10 questions could even find 1 out of 1,024!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Try halving: 8, then 4, then…

clue_cards.name: Doctor's questions
clue_cards.trick: The doctor asks questions one by one: "Fever? Cough?"
clue_cards.does: Each answer rules out lots of illnesses, so the doctor narrows down what's wrong.

clue_cards.name: Leaf key
clue_cards.trick: Scientists ask yes/no questions like "Is the edge smooth?"
clue_cards.does: Each answer cuts the choices down until the mystery leaf is named.

clue_cards.name: Spam filter
clue_cards.trick: A decision tree asks: strange link? Unknown sender?
clue_cards.does: It decides spam or not spam for every email, all by itself.

clue_cards.name: Guess Who players
clue_cards.trick: The best players never guess one face first.
clue_cards.does: They ask questions that knock out half the board at once.

predict.prompt: 8 animals: 4 can fly and 4 can't. Good or bad first question? Predict first!
predict.explain: "Can it fly?" splits the 8 animals in half, so it throws away 4 wrong answers at once. "Is it a penguin?" usually rules out just 1, and "Is it an animal?" rules out none!

lab.title: The card-sorting lab
lab.predict: Which first question splits your 8 animal cards most evenly?
options: Is it bigger than a dog?

tool.name: Brainstorm
tool.intro: Brainstorming is how teams find lots of ideas fast, then pick the best ones. Today you'll use all 5 rules to find Pixel's best questions.

parts.name: Quantity
parts.what: Go for lots of ideas, fast.
parts.example: 🍱 20 lunchbox ideas in 5 minutes: colder, bigger, foldable…
parts.starter: In 5 minutes, my yes/no questions are: Does it have fur? Can it…

parts.name: No Judging
parts.what: Every idea is allowed for now.
parts.example: 🍱 A lunchbox that sings? Write it down anyway!
parts.starter: A funny question I'll still write down is…

parts.name: Wild ideas
parts.what: Be brave and try something unusual.
parts.example: 🍱 A lunchbox that grows its own snacks!
parts.starter: My wildest question for Pixel is…

parts.name: Build on ideas
parts.what: Take an idea and add to it.
parts.example: 🍱 A cold lunchbox → a cold lunchbox with an ice-pack lid.

parts.name: Pick the best
parts.what: Test your ideas and keep the winners.
parts.example: 🍱 Keep the 3 lunchbox ideas that fix the most problems.
parts.starter: After testing on my 8 cards, my 3 most even questions are…

sketch_checklist: I put my best first question at the top.
I added a follow-up on each branch until every animal sits alone.
I marked the longest path, my worst case.

test.check_question: Can your tree guess any of the 8 animals in 3 questions or fewer?

reflection.question: AI check: what could go wrong if a tree like yours decided something important, and someone's answer didn't fit any branch?
options: 🌱 Add a new branch for them
